STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plate, medium-large, typically 20-30 cm; a standard dinner-size square plate is about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the pizza slice is roughly 11-12 cm long along its edge and the plate's right edge runs past the slice with room to spare. About 2.3 slice-lengths span the plate width, so width is about 25-27 cm.
Final width: 25 cm (square, area 625 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Caesar-style salad (romaine with dressing, croutons, shaved cheese). Coverage: roughly 35% of the plate area = 219 cm2. Thickness: loose leaves piled, about 3-4 cm at the centre, averaging about 2 cm. Volume = 219 x 2 = 438 ml. Dressed cooked-ish leafy greens, bulk density about 0.4 g/ml (raw greens 0.15 plus dressing and cheese raise it). Grams = 438 x 0.4 ≈ 175 g.
- Pizza, pepperoni: two slices visible, partly overlapping. Footprint about 12% of plate = 75 cm2 total, 2 slices. Using the slice rule: 2 slices x 30 g = 60 g of bread-based dough is too low for a cheese-and-tomato slice; treat by volume: 75 cm2 x 1.5 cm = 112 ml x 0.9 (topped dough, cheese, sauce) ≈ 100 g. Pizza is about 100 g in total, taken as one item.
- Croutons (visible, about 4-5 pieces): about 10 g total.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the salad has a dressing base mixed through the leaves, already counted in the density. No separate base layer under the pizza.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Caesar salad with dressing and cheese: about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Pepperoni pizza: about 270 kcal/100 g.
- Croutons: about 400 kcal/100 g.

Totals: salad 175 g x 1.5 = 263 kcal; pizza 100 g x 2.7 = 270 kcal; croutons 10 g x 4 = 40 kcal. The croutons are already inside the salad weight, so I list them as a separate item at 10 g and reduce the salad to 165 g: 165 g x 1.5 = 248 kcal.

Total: about 275 g, about 560 kcal.
